NUTRITION PLAN
  GOAL Nutrition plan to support cycle-related fatigue, cramping, and training readiness; aligns with training phases and individual flow window.

  GENERAL GUIDELINES
    - Hydration: aim 35-40 ml/kg/day total fluid; adjust for heat and sweating.
    - Electrolytes: ensure daily sodium 3.0-4.0 g, potassium 3.5-4.5 g, magnesium 300-420 mg, calcium 1000-1300 mg as appropriate from food and supplementation if needed. Increase during flow days if cramping occurs.
    - Protein: 1.6-2.2 g/kg/day to support recovery and strength gains.
    - Carbohydrates: 3-5 g/kg/day depending on training load; higher on flow-allowed days with higher energy demand.
    - Fats: balance to meet overall calorie needs; emphasize omega-3 fats for inflammation (fish, flaxseed, chia).
    - Fiber: maintain 25-38 g/day; adjust around dysmenorrhea if GI discomfort occurs.

  CYCLE-SENSITIVE DAILY TARGETS
    - Non-flow days (days without flow-related restrictions): distribute protein ~0.4 g/kg per meal across 3-4 meals; include a pre- and post-workout protein-rich snack or shake.
    - Flow days (days 1-3 of cycle sleep onset): lower high-intensity volume and avoid heavy valsalva; prioritize easily digestible foods and hydrate. Emphasize iron-rich and calcium-rich foods if iron status is a concern.
    - Bedtime: include a slow-diffusion casein protein or dairy-free alternative if needed to sustain overnight amino acid availability.

  PRE- and POST-WORKOUT NUTRITION
    - Pre-workout (60-90 minutes before session): 20-40 g carbohydrate + 10-20 g protein; examples: banana with yogurt, oats with milk, or a smoothie.
    - Post-workout within 60-90 minutes: 0.5-1.0 g/kg carbohydrate + 0.3-0.5 g/kg protein; examples: chocolate milk, fruit + whey, or rice with chicken.

  FLOW-DAY SPECIFIC MODIFICATIONS
    - On days classified as flow days (debilitating days 1-3): if training is feasible, keep intensity at RPE 6-7 or use light bands and mobility. If fatigue is high, switch to a lighter mobility and core-maintenance session instead of full resistance sets.
    - Cramp management: include 1-2 servings of potassium-rich foods (banana, potatoes, yogurt) and magnesium-rich foods (almonds, spinach) or consider 200-400 mg magnesium citrate if cramps persist (after physician guidance).

  SUPPLEMENTATION (only if appropriate and under supervision)
    - Multivitamin-mineral daily to cover micronutrient gaps.
    - Vitamin D3 800-2000 IU daily if deficient or low sun exposure; check with healthcare provider.
    - Omega-3 supplement 1-2 g combined EPA/DHA daily to support inflammation resolution.
    - If iron deficient or symptomatic: consult clinician; avoid iron supplementation without lab confirmation.

  SLEEP AND STRESS
    - Aim 7-9 hours of sleep per night.
    - Include stress-reduction activities; consider diaphragmatic breathing and light mobility if fatigue is high.

  TRAINING NUTRITION SCHEDULE OVER 12 WEEKS
    - Week 1-4: emphasize consistent protein intake around 1.8 g/kg/day and hydration; adjust carbs to fuel sessions; flow days honored with lower intensity as needed.
    - Week 5-8: increase total calories modestly to support higher volume; ensure post-workout nutrition within 60-90 minutes.
    - Week 9-12: continue progressive overload with balanced nutrition; monitor cramps and energy, adjust electrolytes and minerals accordingly.

 NOTES
  - Modify any exercise if pain or cramping worsens; substitute safe alternatives from canonical list (e.g., replace high-intensity components on flow days with mobility or core work).
  - The nutrition plan should be revisited with a clinician if cramps persist or fatigue worsens.

    - Non-flow days: protein ~0.4 g/kg per meal; include pre-/post-workout protein.
    - Flow days: lower high-intensity; emphasize easily digestible foods; iron/calcium rich focus.
    - Test days: prioritize carbohydrates pre-test; ensure adequate sleep and hydration.
  PRE- and POST-WORKOUT NUTRITION
    - Pre-workout: 20-40 g carbs + 10-20 g protein
    - Post-workout: 0.5-1.0 g/kg carbs + 0.3-0.5 g/kg protein
  FLOW-DAY SPECIFIC MODIFICATIONS
    - Flow days keep intensity at RPE 6-7; adjust macros as needed.
  SUPPLEMENTATION
    - As previously outlined; test-related adjustments only after clinician guidance.
  SLEEP AND STRESS
    - 7-9 hours; diaphragmatic breathing and mobility as needed
  TRAINING NUTRITION SCHEDULE OVER 12 WEEKS
    - Week 1-4: ~1.8 g/kg/day protein; cycle through carbs
    - Week 5-8: calories increased for higher volume
    - Week 9-12: maintain balance; monitor cramps and energy
  HIIT NOTES
    - Slot on non-flow days or replace with mobility if needed
  NOTES
    - 1RM testing only with clinician clearance; align with end-phase Phase 3
    - Modify any exercise if pain/cramps worsen; use canonical substitutions
    - Revisit nutrition with clinician if cramps persist

  ADDITIONAL ATHLETIC/POWER DAY NOTES
    - Plyometric/power blocks integrated in Phase 2 and Phase 3; choose low-to-moderate impact options if flow days constrain jumping

  TESTING PROCEDURE (Phase 3 end)
    - 1RM tests on squat, bench_press, and barbell_row only if medically cleared
    - If not cleared, perform velocity-based or 3RM/GPP-based max effort assessment with proper warmup and technique coaching

  SAFETY AND CONTRAINDICATIONS
    - Flow days avoid high Valsalva, jumping, and high-intensity; adjust test or skip
    - Dysmenorrhea symptoms monitored; adjust session load and conditioning accordingly
